title: Brass bands and funerals; Foster's tuba playing to 1928
summary: Brass bands made the money and played funerals; Foster later played tuba and why he could not fake on it, then left Chicago for Duke Jackson in St. Louis and Louis Russell.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Did they ever have brass bands up there, parades?

Well, the brass bands made more money in them days, and the orchestra made it these days. But they played at funerals. They had parades all through the week. See? Because back in them days they'd bury people on Sunday any other day, didn't they? Because now they tell me they all don't bury on Sunday no more. Sometimes, not all the time.
Sometimes they're better than what they do.

With music? Yeah. They still had music in New Orleans. I saw one last summer. Yeah. See now. The Eureka plays them. Yeah. You see, with the brass bands up here, see they had the guy with the stick. There wasn't no stick. That trumpet player left that brass band. Trumpet player. Wasn't no man. He had to blow something. He had to do something. Did you ever play in brass bands with your two bands? Bass drums. No, I played, in 28 I played the tuba. See when I left home I wasn't playing the tuba. That's why when I went home the guys were surprised when they see me with the tuba. But I didn't play on the stick on the tuba long enough. I was doing very good on the tuba. See? But I couldn't fake nothing on the tuba. That was funny wasn't it? I couldn't fake nothing on the tuba man.

See? Because I started out on the tuba with the music. See? And the last I played in 28, I was writing this very time here. I left Los Angeles playing tuba. And then tuba. Went on the tuba. Went on through. That's when I left the band in Chicago. That's where Johnny had all those kids and women to stay in Chicago. When the name was up on the wall, when they get out of you and get a job. But they want me to stay there. I said no man, you can't take care of me. So I had a job at St. Louis. I went on with Duke Jackson. I stayed with him from September until February. Then Louis Russell sent sent for me. They had sent for me. But too much of that. But Johnny, the guy had all that booking around there. He wouldn't give me the telegram. I sent a telegram to him, but he wouldn't give it to me. Until he and his wife got assaulted, then he'd give me the telegram. See?
